answers.q: Is there evidence of a long-run relationship?
answers.answer: Yes in the linear ARDL: F = 7.54 exceeds the 5% I(1) bound (4.35) and t = -3.83 lies below its I(1) bound (-3.78). In the NARDL, the F-test rejects (F = 5.36) but the t-test does not (t = -2.39 vs -3.99), so the asymmetric long-run relationship is supported by one of the two PSS tests only.

Yes. A permanent 1% depreciation is associated with a 0.53% higher food CPI in the long run (p = 0.043; 95% CI 0.02 to 1.04). The linear ARDL gives 0.64 (p = 0.004). The sign is positive in 12/12 robustness specifications and significant at 5% in 9.
answers.strength: robust in sign; significant in most specifications

answers.q: Does appreciation have an equivalent opposite effect?
answers.answer: Not demonstrably. The long-run appreciation coefficient (1.18, p = 0.29) is statistically indistinguishable from zero and is significant in 0 of 12 specifications. Long-run symmetry is NOT rejected (Wald χ²(1) = 0.47, p = 0.49); it is rejected in 1 of 12 specifications (Sample 2019M07–2025M12 (2015-16-base national CPI only)). Short-run (impact) symmetry IS rejected (F = 5.35, p = 0.023; rejected in 8/12 specifications): in the month the rupee appreciates, food prices do not fall — the point estimate implies they edge up (0.46% per 1% appreciation) before reversing.
answers.strength: short-run asymmetry significant; long-run asymmetry not established

answers.q: Which variables have statistically significant effects?
answers.answer: Long run (ARDL): exchange rate 0.64 (p = 0.004) and FAO food prices 0.61 (p = 0.002); transport CPI 0.21 is not significant (p = 0.36). In the NARDL, transport CPI becomes significant (0.50, p = 0.031) and FAO prices are marginal (p = 0.066).

The linear ARDL passes both CUSUM and CUSUM-of-squares. The NARDL passes CUSUM (within bounds) but its CUSUM-of-squares crosses the 5% band (max deviation 0.378 vs 0.174, around 2017-02), signalling a change in residual variance over the sample (consistent with calm 2015–18 and volatile 2022–25 food prices).

The positive depreciation pass-through survives alternative lag rules, energy and global-food proxies, an outlier dummy and sub-samples in sign (12/12) and mostly in significance (9/12). It weakens when a 2019M07 step dummy and other event dummies are added, because the rebasing step absorbs part of the level shift.
